name: Onyx
notes: Stomp-tempo mosh rap, and the two parameters that make it are a kick on 1 and 3 — beat 3, not the and-of-3 the rest of this axis uses, so `secondaryAnchor` is `3` — and open hats on the offbeats at a probability nothing else here comes near. At 95–105 the 8th hats read as drive rather than swing, so `swing` drops to 0.52 while the tempo band is the fastest on the axis. Harmony is described as "nearly absent": a single distorted guitar or bass figure, static `i` or the Phrygian flat-2. ⚠ **The flat-2 is spelled `II` and the scale table is Phrygian-led, because that is how the engine reaches it.** There is no `bII` roman in this dataset's vocabulary; in a Phrygian model the major chord on the flat second degree *is* `II`, so setting the mode is what makes the chord real rather than a spelling. ⛔ `chords.impliedByRiff` is set as a description of "harmony is nearly absent", and its variety comes from `chordDurationBeats` plus three `harmonicRhythm` values rather than from families it does not play. ⚠ The research says "no counter-melody" — density comes from the vocals. The countermelody block is still authored at `densityRatio` 0.32 with two styles, because that is the floor at which the generated part stays distinct across seeds; read it as the lowest the engine allows rather than as a claim that a counterline is on the record. ⚠ `medium`, and the research marks the drum specifics `[LOW-CONF]` in particular: the production workflow detail is thin, so the kick density, the ghost rate and the open-hat probability are inferences from the record-level description, not from a producer account. ⚠ The bass ceiling came down from 45 to 42 so it stays under a chord part that starts at 43 — `coherence.rs` requires the highest bass note to sit at or below the lowest chord note, and this model overlapped by 3. ⚠ **The 1-bar phrase length was removed** (was [1,2,4], now [2,4]). A one-bar phrase looped four times carries less entropy than a four-bar phrase, and it is the countermelody it strangles hardest: a counter answers *inside* the melody’s phrase, so a one-bar shape leaves it nowhere to go. Every worst offender on `counter.rs` carried it. ⛔ The previous session recorded this exact mistake and it arrived again from the other direction — distinctness is combinatorial in the shape LENGTH, not in the option count.
